title: *Ride Review after 1000 miles* $3500 ELVES FALATH EVO CHINA BIKE

takeaways.text: Frameset supplied free by Elves. Listed at US$1,300 (on sale at US$1,100) in late 2023; the integrated bar added US$110 at checkout instead of US$280, custom paint US$50 more, with a five-year warranty for the first owner.

PF30 bottom bracket (an Elves BB is included) and a 32 mm tire limit per the brand; the shop-owner reviewer had no fitting issues with a third-party thread-together PF30 bottom bracket on several Falath EVO frames.
At about 183 cm he normally rides a 56 but found the 54 (medium) fitted well, and suggests most riders size down.

Faults on his frame: front caliper rub caused by a paint or carbon burr on the mount (sanded off), a very tight bar-end plug, some seatpost slip after repeated height changes, and a stripped small bolt on the seat-clamp cover.

After about 1,000 miles: stiff, responsive and fast at 26–30 mph on flat group rides, but harsh on rides over about 60 miles, which he attributes to the square aero seatpost and low vertical compliance even with 28 mm tires at 85 psi.

disclosure: The description promotes discount codes and commercial product links. Elves-specific frame-supply or payment terms are not established there.
summary: Falath EVO ride review framed around 1,000 miles on a 2023 custom build. It complements the frame assessment without establishing current prices or EVO+ specifications.
